# mfrmr

[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-mfrmr-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/mfrmr)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/mfrmr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/mfrmr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/mfrmr/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/mfrmr/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

**Account for rater differences. Plan your assessment. Report the
results.**

The same performance can receive different scores from different raters.
For speaking performances, essays and other rated work, `mfrmr` helps
you:

- **Measure performance:** estimate person ability while accounting for
  rater severity and task or criterion difficulty.
- **Plan ratings:** compare what adding raters or tasks would do to
  score precision.
- **Explain results:** examine agreement and prepare tables, figures and
  reports for researchers or raters.

[![Three ggplot examples: rater severity with intervals, task/rater
planning curves, and score-category probabilities. All use synthetic
data.](reference/figures/visual-gallery.png)](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/visual-gallery.html)

**[Explore the interactive
gallery](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/visual-gallery.html)**:
inspect values, compare rating plans, and reuse the ggplot2 code in your
report.

## Install the version used here

**These examples require the unreleased 0.2.4 candidate.** If the
maintainer has supplied its `.tar.gz` archive, select it here:

``` r

install.packages(file.choose(), repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

Source installation requires R build tools. Keep the archive and
checksum: different candidates share version `0.2.4`. Without the
candidate, use `install.packages("mfrmr")` for the CRAN release and
follow its installed tutorials via `browseVignettes("mfrmr")`; some
features below will be unavailable.

## Try one assessment

Start with synthetic data for **48 people, six raters and three
criteria**. Each person is assigned two raters; 282 of 288 planned
ratings are observed. Here, interpret 1 as lower performance and 4 as
higher performance.

``` r

library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
head(ratings[c("Person", "Rater", "Criterion", "Score")], 3)
```

| Person | Rater | Criterion    | Score |
|--------|-------|--------------|-------|
| P001   | R01   | Language     | 4     |
| P001   | R01   | Organization | 2     |
| P001   | R02   | Content      | 4     |

**One row is one observed rating.** Missing ratings are absent rows, not
zeros. A *facet* is a source of variation: here, the rater and
assessment criterion.

Fit a rating-scale model (RSM), which uses shared category steps across
criteria, by marginal maximum likelihood (MML). For your assessment, see
the [model-choice
guide](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-model-choice.html).

``` r

fit <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"), score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML", model = "RSM"
)

analysis <- mfrm_results(fit, include = "publication")  # Gather diagnostics and tables
check <- summary(analysis)
check$decision[, c("FormalInference", "NextAction")]
```

Here, `FormalInference` is `Yes`: the implemented inference checks pass.
If it is `No` for your data, follow `NextAction` before making
inferential claims. Passing these checks does not establish construct
validity.

## Read the first figure

``` r

plot(fit, show_ci = FALSE)
```

![Wright map from the synthetic example: person estimates on the left,
rater and criterion locations in the middle, and shared category steps
on the right; confidence intervals are not
shown.](reference/figures/readme-wright.png)

Wright map from the synthetic example: person estimates on the left,
rater and criterion locations in the middle, and shared category steps
on the right; confidence intervals are not shown.

Start with **Rater**: R01 is about −0.61 and R06 about +0.41 logits.
Higher rater locations mean lower expected scores for the same person
and criterion, so R06 is estimated to score more strictly. Zero is a
centered reference, not a quality standard; point estimates alone do not
establish a statistically significant difference. The IQR bars describe
spread, not uncertainty.

The left panel shows person estimates; other columns show criteria and
category steps. See the [visual
guide](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-visual-diagnostics.html).
State what high scores mean: *difficulty in understanding* and *ease of
understanding* run in opposite directions.

## Make a report and keep the analysis

``` r

report <- mfrm_report(analysis, style = "apa", output = "html")
browseURL(report$path)  # Open the draft report in your browser
export_mfrm_results(analysis, output_dir = "assessment-export", preset = "starter")
```

The report combines results, checks and draft wording; the export saves
tables, available figures and a reloadable analysis. Open
`assessment-export/index.html` to navigate the saved files. Add your
study question, sampling, rubric and interpretation. Review person-level
information before sharing.

The [reporting
guide](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-reporting-and-apa.html)
introduces three editable manuscript templates:

| Your question | Template |
|----|----|
| Report a one-family GPCM analysis | `gpcm-report.Rmd`: measures, precision, fit, agreement and figures. |
| Compare rater/task plans | `gtheory-report.Rmd`: sources of variation, plans and uncertainty. |
| Review anchors, bias or model choice | `assessment-review.Rmd`: select the relevant modules. |

Templates require R Markdown and Pandoc; the HTML report above does not.
The guide distinguishes separation, Strata and reliability from observed
agreement (Krippendorff’s alpha and pairwise Cohen’s kappa).

## Choose your next task

| Task | Guide |
|----|----|
| Use your own CSV | [Data-to-report workflow](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-workflow.html) |
| Plan the number of raters or tasks | [G-theory and assessment design](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-gtheory.html) |
| Review agreement and rater differences | [Agreement](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-rating-agreement.html); [rater intervals](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-facet-intervals.html) |
| Check rating links; explore residual patterns | [Networks and reporting](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-networks-and-reporting.html) |
| Choose a model | [Model choice](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-model-choice.html); [GPCM scope](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-gpcm-scope.html) |
| Reuse a calibration or move from other software | [Portable calibration](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-portable-calibration.html); [FACETS migration](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-facets-migration.html); [`?build_conquest_overlap_bundle`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/build_conquest_overlap_bundle.md) |
| Continue in Stan/brms and report saved estimates | [Model export](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/export_mfrm_model.html); [return to figures and reports](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/read_mfrm_posterior.html) |

In R, use `mfrmr_output_guide("beginner")` to choose an entry point. The
public website may be older; `browseVignettes("mfrmr")` matches your
installation.

## Updating, scope and citation

Installing a new version does not update saved calculations. Keep
originals and follow
[NEWS](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/NEWS.md) and **Updating
saved analyses for 0.2.4** in
[`help("mfrmr_workflow_methods")`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrmr_workflow_methods.md).
For retired drawing helpers, see
[`help("mfrmr_plot_migration")`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrmr_plot_migration.md);
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) is the main
entry point.

Native measurement models use one ordered score scale and one latent
person dimension. Two-family GPCM and other experimental routes have
separate limits in the model guides. G/D studies concern variation in
defined observed scores. The
[roadmap](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/ROADMAP.md) separates
current capabilities from future work.

Use `citation("mfrmr")` and the methodological references in the
relevant help. Licensed under the [MIT
License](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT).

`mfrmr` has benefited from discussion and methodological input from
[Dr. Atsushi Mizumoto](https://mizumot.com/) and [Dr. Taichi
Yamashita](https://kugakujo.kansai-u.ac.jp/html/100000882_en.html).

## Rating design and linking networks

Review who rated what, crossing/nesting and observed linking
vulnerabilities. Start with observed ratings or a planned roster;
inspect graph links before fitting, then check model identification.

- [`analyze_hierarchical_structure()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/analyze_hierarchical_structure.md)
  : Analyze the hierarchical structure of a rating design
- [`detect_facet_nesting()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/detect_facet_nesting.md)
  : Detect nesting structure between facets
- [`facet_small_sample_review()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/facet_small_sample_review.md)
  : Review rating counts for each facet level
- [`subset_connectivity_report()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/subset_connectivity_report.md)
  : Build a subset connectivity report (preferred alias)
- [`mfrm_network_analysis()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_network_analysis.md)
  : Analyze the MFRM design network
- [`build_mfrm_network_review()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/build_mfrm_network_review.md)
  : Build an MFRM network review
- [`build_peer_review_sim_spec()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/build_peer_review_sim_spec.md)
  : Build a peer-review simulation specification
- [`review_peer_design()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/review_peer_design.md)
  : Review a peer-assessment assignment design

## G-theory assessment planning

Separate observed-score variation, project specified future plans, and
compare eligible prespecified plans. Start with the G-theory planning
article.

- [`mfrm_g_study()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_g_study.md)
  [`print(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_gstudy>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_g_study.md)
  [`summary(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_gstudy>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_g_study.md)
  : G-study for one or several observed scores
- [`confint(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_gstudy>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy.md)
  : Sampling uncertainty in G-study variance and covariance components
- [`vcov(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_gstudy>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/vcov.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy.md)
  : Sampling covariance and SEs of G-study component estimates
- [`plot(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_gstudy>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/plot.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy.md)
  : Inspect sources of observed-score variation
- [`mfrm_d_study()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_d_study.md)
  [`print(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_d_study>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/mfrm_d_study.md)
  : Plan measurement conditions with a D-study
- [`summary(`*`<mfrm_multivariate_d_study>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/reference/summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study.md)
  : Summarize assessment plans with their uncertainty

  probabilities](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/visual-gallery.md):

  the values behind each figure.
